candidate.title: smMIP
candidate.scope: Single Molecule Molecular Inversion Probes (smMIP; smMIPs in the explanatory label), specifically the smMIP row of the assigned Illumina DNA Low-Level Detection schematic, interpreted using the original Hiatt et al. implementation where chemistry or read identity needs clarification. One linear capture-to-consensus route is depicted; the Gene icon identifies the biological target rather than a separate workflow. The NS-seq row above, MIPSTR row below, and partial chemical legend at right are neighboring context with no connecting arrows to smMIP. They are not alternative targets of this card. The extraction describes tagged target-copy circles and their library/readout, not a complete execution protocol or every application discussed in the catalogue.

operations.label: Genomic DNA (probe hybridization depicted)
operations.description: Bring the smMIP arms into sequence-specific association with genomic regions flanking the target. The input DNA and tagged probe become a hybridized probe-template complex ready for copying. The initial Gene icon is explanatory target context, not a transfer from the neighboring assay.
operations.mechanism: Complementary targeting arms hybridize to flanking genomic sequences. The primary describes pooled probes; the schematic illustrates a representative complex.
operations.information_effect: Probe-arm specificity selects the genomic interval to be represented. The molecular tag resides on the probe that will carry the target copy.

operations.label: Copy target sequence
operations.description: Use the bound genomic template to fill the gap in the probe and ligate the completed probe into a single-stranded circle. The output reaction contains tagged circles carrying target-sequence copies alongside residual genomic DNA and unclosed probes.
operations.mechanism: Polymerase copies the reverse complement of the intervening genomic sequence and ligase closes the probe into a circle. These enzymes are catalysts in this local operation, not separate material-transfer branches.
operations.information_effect: Physical linkage of the copied target and pre-existing molecular tag records a capture event before PCR duplication. The sequenced target information is carried by probe-derived DNA.

operations.label: Exonuclease
operations.description: Digest uncircularized probes and genomic DNA remaining in the capture reaction, enriching the intact tagged target-copy circles that proceed to PCR. The primary resolves the retained product where the poster draws a dotted upper loop.
operations.mechanism: Exonuclease digestion degrades uncircularized probe and genomic DNA after gap-fill and ligation. The intact target-bearing circle is retained as the amplification template.
operations.information_effect: Enriches circular capture products while retaining the target-copy/tag association. Survival is not a test of whether an observed sequence variant is biological.

operations.label: Corrected sequence
operations.description: Call one consensus target sequence from each aligned read family. The diagram retains the consistently represented True variant and removes scattered Random error marks. The primary excludes synthetic targeting-arm bases from the biological consensus.
operations.mechanism: Family-based single molecule consensus calling reduces random library-construction and sequencing errors using repeated observations of the captured sequence.
operations.information_effect: Supports detection and estimation of low-frequency target variants using captured-copy consensuses rather than treating every PCR descendant as an independent target molecule. It does not guarantee an error-free biological sequence: initial gap-fill errors and template damage can persist.

method_scopes.rationale: All operations belong to the one smMIP row identified by the card and by the image label, including the implied sequencing interface. Single Molecule Molecular Inversion Probes / smMIPs is the expanded name/plural of smMIP, not another target method. The verified catalogue page has the same smMIP heading and sequence of labels, and Hiatt et al. Figure 1 supports the tagged-circle-to-consensus architecture. The adjacent NS-seq and MIPSTR workflows are separately labeled rows, not alternatives within the assigned smMIP schematic. Primary details clarify this depicted implementation without asserting that every smMIP application has an identical complete protocol.

checks.rationale: Independent inspection supports this smMIP architecture at the declared schematic/Hiatt-clarified implementation scope. Every in-scope transformation and retained route is represented, with no additional target method imported from adjacent rows or catalogue applications. Biological genomic template, synthetic tagged target-copy carrier, amplified library and read/consensus data remain distinct. The only multi-input operation, op_capture, is genuine probe-template association; no separately processed branches or compartments have been collapsed. checks.rationale: The correction accurately records the visible ambiguity: dotted upper probe arc and genomic line with lower colored segments retained. Matching smMIP full text states that the gap-filled/ligated product is a single-stranded circle and that exonuclease degrades uncircularized probes and genomic DNA. Retaining intact target-copy circles is therefore a supported interpretation, not an unexplained biological impossibility. The candidate preserves the diagram observation and applies the resolution consistently in op_exonuclease, s_captured, s_selected, f_06/f_07/f_08 and op_pcr; no incompatible backbone-deleted route remains.
